payload.title: The agent places. A program does the pixel arithmetic and checks it
payload.why: #vi-sysdiag-svg read well because the agent chose the lanes and the order, not because the SVG was hand-tuned. The hand-tuning is the cost: in .werk/diagram-a.svg the agent computed 22 label plates as chars * 5.6 + 8 and 22 box borders by hand. That arithmetic is mechanical, it is where the spacing errors came from, and a program does it exactly.
payload.body:
Split the drawing in two, along the line the prototype already drew.

**Intent (the agent writes it).** Which lane a node sits in, which order inside the lane, which nodes group, which of the seven edge colours an edge carries, and the label text. This is judgement. Mermaid failed at exactly this, because its auto-layout took the choice away — see #vi-sysdiag-svg.

**Arithmetic (a program does it).** Text measurement, box size from text, label plate size and centring, lane box size from its contents, the point where an arrow meets a border, grid spacing, and the viewBox. None of this needs judgement. All of it was done by hand in `.werk/diagram-a.svg`, 44 times.

The program is a resolver over a grid, not a layout engine. It never chooses which node goes where. Given lane + index it computes x and y. That is the difference from #vi-sysdiag-format:opt0, which was rejected as "layout code" when the assumption was still that some program must decide positions.

Text measurement has an exact answer here: werk renders its own picture in a browser, so the renderer runs client-side and calls `measureText`. No font metrics table, no `chars * 5.6` estimate.

Open: which option below. See the three `alternative_to` options.

payload.title: Fork Mermaid, or write a custom Mermaid renderer
payload.why_not: The failure in #vi-sysdiag-svg was auto-layout, not rendering. Mermaid's syntax cannot carry lane, order, or edge colour class, so a custom renderer either re-derives positions (the same failure) or needs the syntax extended anyway. Extending it costs more than a new format.

payload.title: A skill file only: write the spacing rules in markdown, let the agent do the arithmetic
payload.why_not: The arithmetic in prose is what produced the errors. An agent multiplying 19 characters by 5.6 for 22 labels is the baby-sitting, not a fix for it. It also breaks the rule that logic goes in a program and markdown holds prompt text only.

payload.title: A constrained auto-layout engine (ELK, dagre with lane constraints)
payload.why_not: It chooses positions again. The prototype's whole result is that agent-chosen placement reads better than solver-chosen placement on this data. Also a large dependency for a tool that has none.

payload.title: A checker reads the drawing back and fails loudly. That is what removes the baby-sitting
payload.why: Nothing told the agent the spacing was wrong. Eryk's eye was the only check. A renderer alone does not fix that: it fixes the errors we predicted, not the ones we did not. A checker that the agent runs after each redraw closes the loop without a human in it.
payload.body:
The checker reads the intent file and the resolved geometry, and reports, as text the agent can act on:

1. Two boxes overlap, or a box overlaps a lane frame.
2. Text is wider than its box, or a label plate is wider than its edge run.
3. An edge crosses another edge, or passes through a box it does not connect.
4. An edge has no label, or a node has no card id.
5. Anything is outside the viewBox.

The agent redraws until the checker is silent. Eryk sees only the clean result.

Rules 1, 2 and 5 are errors: the resolver should make them impossible, so one firing is a resolver bug. Rule 3 is a warning, because some crossings are correct. Rule 4 catches a fold that dropped content, which is the failure #vi-sysdiag-proto is actually testing for.

See #vi-sysdiag-render for the split this sits inside.

payload.title: The intent file: nested groups, rows, and edges with a colour class. Eight keywords
payload.why: The agent's judgement in #vi-sysdiag-svg was: which lane, which order, which group, which colour. That fits in about 40 lines of text. Everything else in the 264-line SVG was arithmetic. The format exists to carry only the first part.
payload.body:
Replaces the Mermaid file of #vi-sysdiag-format. One file, still hand-editable, still diffs line by line, still carries the card ids inline as #vi-sysdiag-backedge wants — no separate mapping block now, because the id sits on the node line.

```
group browser "BROWSER"
  group mapview "MAP VIEW"
    row tree "card tree" @vi-onview  graph3d "3D graph" @vi-graph3d
  group chat "CHAT PANE"
    row stream "reply stream" @al-stream  perm "permission gate" @al-perm

group server "SERVER PROCESS"
  row http "http routes" @werk-serve
  row agent "agent loop" @al-loop

group store "STORE"
  row log "log.jsonl" @werk-log

edge tree -> http   : read  "loads the card tree"
edge agent -> log   : write "appends one event"
```

The whole language:

| keyword | what the agent decides |
|---|---|
| `group <id> "<label>"` | what boxes together, and nesting. Indentation is the nesting |
| `row <node> <node> ...` | which nodes sit on one line, left to right, in the order written |
| `<id> "<label>" @<card>` | a node, its text, and the card that decided it |
| `edge a -> b : <class> "<label>"` | the connection, one of seven colour classes, and the label |

No coordinate appears anywhere. No width, no padding, no font size. If a number can be computed, it is not in the file. That is the test for whether a keyword belongs.

The seven classes are the ones already in `.werk/diagram-a.svg`: read, state, agent, perm, write, ext, dev. The class carries meaning, not just colour, so naming it is judgement and it stays in the file.

Reversible, for the same reason #vi-sysdiag-format gave: the fold produces text, and swapping the text format costs one redraw.

payload.title: Seven passes, one direction, no search. That is why it is not a layout engine
payload.why: #vi-sysdiag-format:opt0 rejected a custom format because it implied layout code. The rejection assumed a program must decide positions. It does not: given lane and index from #vi-sysdiag-intent, x and y are arithmetic.
payload.body:
The resolver turns the intent file into geometry. It runs once, top to bottom. No iteration, no constraint solving, no crossing minimisation, no force simulation.

1. Measure every label, in the real font.
2. Node box = text width + padding. Height is fixed per nesting level.
3. Row width = sum of its boxes + gaps. A group inner width = its widest row.
4. A group box = inner size + padding + the header line. Nested groups roll up, innermost first.
5. Assign absolute x and y, outermost first, stacking rows with a fixed gap and centring each row.
6. Per edge: pick the two anchor sides from relative position, route orthogonally, place the label plate on the midpoint of the longest straight run, size the plate from the measured label.
7. viewBox = bounding box + margin.

Nothing in that list makes a choice. Every step has one answer. A layout engine is a search over positions, and there is no search here, because #vi-sysdiag-intent already fixed the order.

Cost: about 300 lines, plus 80 for the parser. The checker in #vi-sysdiag-lint is separate.

How to know it works: it must reproduce `.werk/diagram-a.svg` from about 40 lines of intent. That file is the target output, not a starting point — it is already the drawing Eryk accepted.

payload.title: Text width must be exact in Node and in the browser, or pass 1 of the resolver lies
payload.why: The current SVG sets font-family ui-sans-serif,system-ui, which resolves to a different font on a different machine. The hand estimate chars * 5.6 was wrong before anyone typed it. The checker in #vi-sysdiag-lint runs in Node, where there is no measureText, so both sides must agree or the check is worthless.
payload.body:
Every box size in #vi-sysdiag-resolve comes from pass 1. If pass 1 is an estimate, every later number inherits the error, and the checker cannot tell a real overlap from a measurement error.

Two ways to make it exact. Pick one.

**A. Embed one font as a data URI, measure from its metrics.** The SVG carries the font, so it renders the same on any machine and in any viewer. Widths come from the font tables, in Node and in the browser, from the same code. Cost: one font file in the repo, about 30 to 80 kB in every SVG.

**B. Generate a width table once in the browser, check it in.** A small command opens the page, runs measureText over the printable characters at the three sizes used, and writes a table to src/. Node reads the table. Cost: the table is only right for the machine that made it, so a different system font on Eryks

patch.body:
Every box size in #vi-sysdiag-resolve comes from pass 1. If pass 1 is an estimate, every later number inherits the error, and the checker cannot tell a real overlap from a measurement error.

Two ways to make it exact. Pick one.

**A. Embed one font as a data URI, measure from its metrics.** The SVG carries the font, so it renders the same on any machine and in any viewer. Widths come from the font tables, in Node and in the browser, from the same code. Cost: one font file in the repo, about 30 to 80 kB in every SVG.

**B. Generate a width table once in the browser, check it in.** A small command opens the page, runs measureText over the printable characters at the three sizes used, and writes a table to src/. Node reads the table. Cost: the table is right only for the machine that made it, so a different system font on one laptop and on CI disagree again.

A is the recommended one. It removes the machine from the answer instead of recording one machine answer.

payload.title: Keep a system font stack and approximate the width
payload.why_not: That is what .werk/diagram-a.svg already did, with chars * 5.6 + 8. The plates came out the wrong width, and no check could catch it, because the checker would use the same wrong number.

patch.why:
#vi-prop's 6% to 11% is about recovering edges that were never written. Nothing is being recovered here: the changed card and the whole diagram are both in the agent's context, so the affected elements are read, not inferred. The argument for a mechanical mark returns only when the diagram stops fitting.

Format-independent: the limit is on the diagram text and the card set, not on the picture. It applies the same to the Mermaid render and to #vi-sysdiag-svg.

payload.title: A card that decides a connection gets its own line in a separate '%% edges' block, keyed by the two node ids

patch.body:
One node touches many connections, each decided by a different card. Mixing all of them onto the node's own line loses which arrow is in question. A second comment section fixes this, keyed by the connection itself:

```
%% cards
%% tree: vi-overwrite, vi-onview

%% edges
%% tree->http: vi-onview
```

Still comments, per #vi-sysdiag-format — Mermaid ignores everything after `%%`. A node's `%% cards` line now holds only cards that shaped the box. A card that shaped one connection lives only in `%% edges`, keyed to that arrow.

payload.title: Add the connection-deciding card's id to both endpoint nodes' '%% cards' lines, no separate block
payload.why_not: Once a node has several connections decided by different cards, its line mixes them with the cards that shaped the box itself. The reader must open every card to know which one is in question. Rejected once the diagram in front of us hit that case.

patch.why: Mermaid has no metadata field on a node or an edge, so the id must live in the comment mapping block from #vi-sysdiag-format. A connection is decided by a specific card, not by the two boxes it touches, so it gets its own line, keyed to the two node ids it runs between.

payload.title: D2 grid diagrams: the author declares rows and columns, the tool does not choose
payload.finding: Setting grid-rows or grid-columns on a container switches it out of Dagre/ELK graph layout into a grid the author controls. Grids nest, and a grid cell can hold a normal diagram. Connections between cells work normally. Two limits: a column forces one width and a row forces one height on all its members, which produces the empty space Mermaid produced; and under Dagre or ELK an edge inside a grid is a centre-to-centre straight segment with no path-finding.

payload.title: D2 subsets the font into the SVG and measures text from that font, not from the browser
payload.finding: The SVG renderer embeds the font as base64 to give deterministic output and to load with no network call. Layout dimensions come from the embedded font's metrics, not from getBBox, so the measured box and the drawn text agree on any machine. Since 0.3.0 only the used glyphs are embedded: SVG size fell to about 5% of the 0.2 size.

payload.title: @terrastruct/d2: the whole of D2 as WASM, in Node and in the browser, one API
payload.finding: d2.compile(text) then d2.render() returns an SVG string. The same code runs in Node and in the browser. It calls the WASM build through a web worker, and loads from a CDN via esm.sh, which is how werk already loads 3d-force-graph.

payload.title: TALA, D2's architecture-diagram layout and edge-routing engine, became MPL-2.0 in September 2026
payload.finding: Open-sourced under MPL-2.0 around 2026-09-08 and bundled with D2 0.9.0 and later. No licence key, no token, no watermark. Selected with --layout=tala. It is the one D2 layout engine that routes an edge inside a grid instead of drawing a centre-to-centre line.

payload.title: satori: HTML and CSS to SVG, with a flexbox engine and font metrics, no browser
payload.finding: Takes a JSX tree and returns an SVG string. Layout is Yoga, the flexbox engine. Text is measured with opentype.js from a font you pass in, and a font is mandatory. It renders text as path by default, so the output needs no font files. It has no notion of an edge, an arrow, or a connector.

payload.title: libavoid: optimal object-avoiding orthogonal connector routing, with a WASM port
payload.finding: Wybrow, Marriott and Stuckey, GD 2009. Three stages: build an orthogonal visibility graph, find the route by A* over it, then centre and nudge the routes. It minimises a function of length and bend count and is optimal, not a heuristic, in O(n^2 log n) per connector. The paper's stated target is editors whose ad-hoc heuristics send routes through objects. libavoid-js is an Emscripten port, 8 to 11 times slower than native, which is still nothing at 22 edges. LGPL 2.1.

payload.title: Edge crossings are the aesthetic that hurts comprehension most, measured
payload.finding: Purchase, Cohen and James, and Purchase 1997, Which aesthetic has the greatest effect on human understanding? Of five aesthetics tested, minimising edge crossings was by far the most important for reading a graph. Bends came second. Later work refines it: Ware et al. found the crossings that matter are the ones on the path the reader is following, not the total count.

payload.title: Penrose: Substance says what exists, Style says how it looks, and Substance holds no numbers
payload.finding: SIGGRAPH 2020, Carnegie Mellon. Three languages: Domain defines the vocabulary, Substance declares objects and relations only, Style turns them into shapes and positions. Penrose has no numeric type in Substance at all — you cannot write a coordinate there even if you want to. One Substance file renders two ways under two Style files. Positions come from minimising a badness function, which is the part that does not transfer.

payload.title: Structurizr keeps hand placement out of the DSL, and loses it when the DSL changes
payload.finding: Simon Brown, the author of the C4 model, on why manual layout exists: architecture diagrams are storytelling tools and are often more effective when placement is precise. Structurizr is unusual among diagrams-as-code tools in supporting both. The failure mode is the warning: x and y live in a separate workspace JSON, not in the DSL, so reordering lines in the DSL loses an element's layout because it can no longer be matched. Use explicit keys.

payload.title: Graphviz has had place-then-render as a supported mode since the 1990s: neato -n2
payload.finding: neato -n2 takes every node's pos as given, does no layout and no overlap removal, routes only the edges that have no pos, and emits. The unit trap is documented: pos is inches normally but points under -n, so set inputscale=72. Prior art that the split in this card is a normal shape for a diagram tool, not an invention.

payload.title: Buy the resolver instead of writing it: D2 grid layout plus TALA routing
payload.why: This option did not exist when #vi-sysdiag-render was written. D2 grid takes the placement from the author, not from a solver, which is the one property that made #vi-sysdiag-svg read well. TALA, which routes edges instead of drawing centre-to-centre lines, became MPL-2.0 on 2026-09-08 and ships in D2 0.9.0. Together they cover all seven passes of #vi-sysdiag-resolve.
payload.body:
What it replaces, pass by pass:

| #vi-sysdiag-resolve pass | D2 |
|---|---|
| 1 measure text | font subset embedded in the SVG, measured from its own metrics — see #d2-fonts. This also answers #vi-sysdiag-metrics, option A, for free |
| 2 to 5 boxes, rows, groups, coordinates | `grid-rows` / `grid-columns` on a container, nested — see #d2-grid |
| 6 route edges and place labels | TALA — see #tala |
| 7 viewBox | done |

The intent file of #vi-sysdiag-intent stays, near enough: containers nest, connection labels and classes exist, and a card id fits in a node attribute. It becomes D2 syntax instead of eight keywords werk owns.

Two things decide this, and neither is settled:

1. **The equal-cell rule.** A D2 grid column forces one width on every member, and a row forces one height. That is how Mermaid produced the empty regions Eryk rejected in #vi-sysdiag-svg. The documented workaround is invisible spacer elements, which is hand-tuning under a different name. Whether it bites depends on how uneven the labels are — and in `.werk/diagram-a.svg` they are very uneven, from "log.jsonl" to "streams the reply as written".
2. **The dependency.** werk has none, and no build step. D2 arrives as a WASM blob plus a web worker — see #d2-js. The checker of #vi-sysdiag-lint would also have to read D2 output rather than werk geometry, because werk would no longer know where anything is.

Cheap to settle: write `.werk/diagram-a.svg` as D2 with grid-rows, render it with `--layout=tala`, and put it beside the hand SVG. That is an hour, and it answers point 1 with a picture instead of an argument.

patch.body:
The checker reads the intent file and the resolved geometry, and reports, as text the agent can act on:

1. Two boxes overlap, or a box overlaps a lane frame.
2. Text is wider than its box, or a label plate is wider than its edge run.
3. An edge crosses another edge, or passes through a box it does not connect.
4. An edge has no label, or a node has no card id.
5. Anything is outside the viewBox.

The agent redraws until the checker is silent. Eryk sees only the clean result.

Rules 1, 2 and 5 are errors: the resolver should make them impossible, so one firing is a resolver bug. Rule 4 catches a fold that dropped content, which is the failure #vi-sysdiag-proto is actually testing for.

Rule 3 was going to be a warning. #purchase-aesthetics says otherwise: of five aesthetics tested, edge crossings hurt comprehension by far the most, with bends second. So the crossing count is the main number the checker reports, and the agent is expected to act on it. Ware et al. refine it further — the crossings that cost the reader are the ones on the path the reader follows — so the count is reported per edge, not only as a total.

See #vi-sysdiag-render for the split this sits inside.

Tried on 2026-09-13. D2 0.9.0 from Homebrew, TALA bundled, renders in 25 to 30 ms. Three variants of the same content as `.werk/diagram-a.svg`, all in `.werk/`: `diagram-a.d2`, `diagram-b.d2`, `diagram-c.d2`, each with its SVG.

**What worked.** Text measurement is exact, every box fits its label, and no label overflows. The order declared with `grid-rows` inside MAP VIEW, CHAT PANE and STORE came out exactly as written. Edge colour classes work. The intent half of #vi-sysdiag-intent survives the translation with almost no loss.

**A, full root grid.** Every top-level container gets the width of the widest one, so `cli`, `claude code child` and `issue tracker` each stretch to 1500 px for a two-line label. 3517 x 2210, against 1800 x 1380 by hand.

**B, grid inside containers, TALA places the top level.** Compact, and the closest to the hand drawing in density. It also overlaps: the STORE frame sits on top of the SERVER PROCESS frame, and three nodes are drawn over the CHAT PANE frame. A solver chose the top-level positions and chose wrong.

**C, root grid with the three loose nodes wrapped in an invisible row.** No overlap, right structure, and the failure is the one Eryk already rejected: the SERVER PROCESS and STORE frames are full width because BROWSER is, so the right half of each is empty. 3536 x 1734, aspect 2.04 against 1.30 by hand. Cross-container edges — "reads every past decision", "runs the agent", "saves the conversation" — route around the outside of the whole canvas instead of through the empty middle.

**The finding.** A D2 grid gives order, not proportion. A column is one width and a row is one height for every member, and there is no column span. The hand drawing reads well partly because the widths are unequal: `http + sse` spans the full server, `cli` is small. That is not expressible, and the documented workaround is invisible spacers, which is hand-tuning under a new name — variants A and C already needed three of them.

So D2 does not replace #vi-sysdiag-resolve. It does settle #vi-sysdiag-metrics: #d2-fonts is the proof that subset-the-font-into-the-SVG works, in a shipping tool.

Open, because rejecting it is Eryks call, not mine. Untried levers: `near` for shape-relative placement, explicit `width` and `height` on containers, and `grid-gap`.

payload.text: Correction to the last line of the body: it should read "rejecting it is your call, not mine". The apostrophe was eaten by the shell.

The style toggle now has a third button, D2 + TALA, beside Mermaid and SVG. It serves .werk/diagram-c-d2.svg, the same nodes and edges rendered by d2 0.9.0. The route reads a query parameter, so it only goes live after the server restarts - #werk-hmr's guard stops a route edit inside serve() from applying hot.

Built. src/sysdiag/{metrics,types,parse,resolve,render,check,build}.ts, plus .werk/diagram-a.intent (the hand-authored intent file) and .werk/font-metrics.json (real widths from headless Chrome canvas measureText, not chars * 5.6 — settles #vi-sysdiag-metrics as option B: table checked in, not embedded per-SVG, because werk still has zero npm dependencies).

`bun src/sysdiag/build.ts .werk/diagram-a.intent .werk/diagram-a-resolved.svg` — 0 errors, 6 warnings, in .werk/diagram-a-resolved.svg. The map has a fourth toggle button, Resolver, to view it (needs a server restart, same #werk-hmr route-handler limit as the D2 button).

What held: text measurement is exact — rule 2 never fired, no title or description line overflows its box, because the box was sized from the same measurement. Rule 1 never fired: no box overlaps another that is not its own group frame. #vi-sysdiag-intent survived close to word for word — 23 lines plus 22 edge lines.

What did not: visually, this reads worse than the hand file. Rule 3 found 3 real edge crossings, which #purchase-aesthetics says is the number that costs a reader the most — but the bigger problem rule 3 cannot see is label clutter: several edge-label plates sit on top of each other or on top of a node, because parallel edges fan in from a wide row onto a narrower one below (9 read-edges from two rows of 4 and 5 converging onto one "http + sse" box) and each label lands at its own edges longest-segment midpoint with no awareness of its neighbors. That is not covered by any of #vi-sysdiag-lints five rules — none of them check a label against another label, or a label against a box it does not belong to.

So the seven passes are not enough. A fan-in of edges onto one node needs a pass that gives them a shared position, the way the hand file put all nine of them in a single label row at one y. That is an eighth thing to decide, not a bug in what is here.

payload.title: A diagram edge marks a conceptual boundary. It does not promise one edge per code route
payload.why: Nine UI elements each draw an edge to the http node, but the code has two channels: one fetch (/api/graph) and one SSE stream (/api/live). #vi-sysdiag-purpose already says the diagram shows the shape we want, not an audit of the code. This is the same rule, stated for edges: grouping several features under one drawn connection is normal, as long as the mapping block names the card that decided each one, per #vi-sysdiag-edgeid.

payload.title: Require one diagram edge per literal code route or call
payload.why_not: The http node would split into /api/graph and /api/live, and every UI element would re-point to whichever it actually calls. That is a code map, the thing #vi-sysdiag-purpose already ruled out as the diagram's job.

payload.text:
Added the eighth pass: a shared lane per row-gap, plus 1D packing when two labels sharing a lane still overlap. Fixed exactly what it was built for — the 9 read-edges into http + sse and the http -> fold/runner fan-out now sit in one clean row each, matching how the hand file placed them. Before and after: /tmp/resolved.png vs the current .werk/diagram-a-resolved.svg.

That surfaced the next problem faster than eyeballing would have: I finished implementing rule 3s other half on #vi-sysdiag-lint — "or passes through a box it does not connect" — which I had specified but never written. It fired 15 times on the first run. Zoomed into one: the line from "refines tree" down to "http + sse" draws straight through the "transcript" box, entering at its top edge and leaving at its bottom, because tree and transcript share an x-column and nothing routes around a box that happens to sit between a source and its target.

This is a different failure than the label clutter. That one was "two correct lines, placed too close." This is "one line, drawn through a box." The seven-plus-one passes here only ever bend a path once, toward the target; they never check whether that bend passes through something. That is exactly the job #libavoid and TALA exist for — optimal object-avoiding routing, found by search over a visibility graph. #vi-sysdiag-resolves "no search" framing holds for placement, not for routing once a diagram has enough rows that a straight bend is likely to cross something.

Implemented: overlap (rule 1), text overflow (rule 2), label plate size formula, edges through boxes and edge crossings (rule 3, both halves), missing label / missing card (rule 4), out of viewBox (rule 5). src/sysdiag/check.ts. Rule 3's box-crossing half is treated as an error, not a warning, unlike the crossing count itself - a line through an unrelated box is a routing defect, not a density tradeoff #purchase-aesthetics would ever accept.

payload.title: libavoid fixes the box-crossing defect. It also breaks the label-placement pass built for a simpler router
payload.why: #vi-sysdiag-resolve's checker found 15 cases of a line drawn through a box it does not connect. That is exactly what #libavoid exists to solve — optimal object-avoiding routing over a visibility graph, not a one-bend guess.
payload.body:
werk now depends on libavoid-js 0.5.0-beta.5 (package.json), for this prototype only — not yet a kept decision. src/sysdiag/route-libavoid.ts replaces pass 6 (routeEdge) only; passes 1 to 5 and 7 (bands, decluttering) are unchanged, per src/sysdiag/resolve.tss new layoutDoc/placeLabels/finishDiagram split.

`bun src/sysdiag/build.ts .werk/diagram-a.intent .werk/diagram-a-libavoid.svg --router=libavoid` — 0 errors (was 15), 8 warnings (was 6; two edges gained one more crossing).

The win is real and checker-confirmed: every "runs through a box" error is gone. tree -> http, which used to draw straight through the transcript box, now bends around it: (238,178) down to (238,219), right to (393,219), down to (393,550), into http. Genuine obstacle-avoiding routing, not a guess.

Unplanned side effect: every edge into a shape shares one registered connection pin (its center, all four directions open), and libavoid routes all of them through a single shared corridor into that point rather than each finding its own nearest side — 9 read-edges into http, and 3 others, all converge and enter from https right side, regardless of whether their source is above, left, or upper-right. This is libavoid choosing one cheap approach for a shared endpoint, not a bug in it. It is a different kind of bundling than #vi-sysdiag-resolves pass 8, discovered for free rather than engineered.

The real defect: pass 7s label placement assumes the routers output looks like the built-in one — one or two bends, the longest segment usually a real gap. libavoids paths bend more and hug box corners tighter, so several labels now land on top of a boxs title or description ("asks before a risky action" sits directly on "http + sse"s title; "streams the reply as written" cuts through its description). Confirmed by cropping and reading the pixels, not inferred.

So: routing, buy. Label placement, not portable to what was bought without more work — it needs to reason about libavoids bend shape, not the built-in routers.

payload.title: A node splits when the picture already implies the boundary the code confirms
payload.why: The 'http + sse' node was one box for two channels: GET /api/graph (one fetch) and POST /api/chat + SSE /api/live (the pane's stream). The flowchart already grouped every consumer into 'map view' and 'chat pane' subgraphs — that grouping is exactly the state/live boundary. #vi-sysdiag-derive's claim 1 says the node fold needs judgement; this is that judgement applied a second time, once the edge work in #vi-sysdiag-boundary made the two channels visible. Split into 'state' and 'live' nodes in .werk/diagram.mmd.

payload.title: Per-side connection pins, not one shared center pin
payload.why: One pin at a box's center, open on all four sides, is why libavoid bundles every incoming edge into one shared corridor and one entry side (#vi-sysdiag-libavoid). Distinct pins per side let each edge attach nearest its own source.
payload.body:
Register four ShapeConnectionPins per box instead of one: top (0.5,0), bottom (0.5,1), left (0,0.5), right (1,0.5), each with visDirs restricted to only that side, same classId. A ConnEnd keeps connecting by classId, so this should not change the call shape in route-libavoid.ts, only the setup loop.

Open question this does not answer up front: does the router pick the geometrically nearest pin per edge on its own, or does something still need to tell it which pin a given ConnEnd should prefer? Find out by running it, not by reading more docs — #vi-sysdiag-protos whole method.

payload.title: Pass 7 has to read libavoid's own bends, not assume the built-in router's
payload.why: Labels landing on box text (#vi-sysdiag-libavoid) happen because pass 7's band lookup assumes a path is one or two segments and the longest one is usually open space. libavoid's paths bend more and hug corners, breaking that assumption.
payload.body:
Minimum fix: before accepting a candidate label position, check it against every box (the same rectangle test #vi-sysdiag-lints rule 3 already has) and reject a position that lands inside one, falling back to the next-longest segment instead of the longest.

This does not require throwing out the band/declutter machinery in resolve.ts — bands and decluttering still apply once a legal (non-overlapping) segment is chosen. It only changes how the segment is chosen.

payload.text: Done. pickLabelSegment now tries candidates longest-first and skips any whose midpoint would land inside a box that isn't its own endpoint (src/sysdiag/resolve.ts). placeLabels re-checks after band-snapping too, since a band good for the built-in router's paths can still land inside a box on libavoid's. Result: 0 rule-3 box-crossing errors, and no label sits on a box's text anymore, confirmed by re-screenshotting .werk/diagram-a-libavoid.svg.

Half done. Four pins per box instead of one fixed the shared-corridor effect - lines now approach from their own natural side. The direction-restricted version (top pin only ConnDirUp, etc.) did not work: libavoid warned 'no pins with class id of 1' for 8 of 9 edges into one box and fell back to routing that ignored obstacles - my ConnDirFlags bit values (1/2/4/8) are probably wrong, or 'visDirs' does not mean what I assumed. Shipped with all four pins open in all directions instead, which still gives the router four positions to pick from by cost. Correct directional restriction is unresolved, not attempted further this round.

Both fixes applied. .werk/diagram-a-libavoid.svg regenerated: 0 rule-3 errors (box crossings and label-on-box both gone), 8 warnings (edge-crossing counts only, which #purchase-aesthetics says to report, not silently fix). Screenshotted and read pixel-by-pixel to confirm, not inferred from the checker alone.

#vi-sysdiag-libavoid-labels is decided: pickLabelSegment skips a candidate segment whose midpoint would land in a box, tried longest-first; placeLabels re-validates after band-snapping for the same reason.

#vi-sysdiag-libavoid-pins is half done: four pins per box beats one shared center pin (edges now approach from their own side, not one shared corridor), but direction-restricted pins (top pin only usable from above, etc.) failed outright - libavoid warned it had no usable pin for 8 of 9 edges into one box and fell back to routing that ignored obstacles. Shipped with all four pins open in every direction instead. The correct ConnDirFlags semantics remain unresolved.

payload.title: Two more keywords: cols for side-by-side groups, !fill for a box that spans its group's width
payload.why: Both MAP VIEW/CHAT PANE and http + sse are stacked-only today because #vi-sysdiag-intent's layout() always stacks a group's children vertically and sizes every box from its own text. Neither restriction is required by the architecture — both are the current resolver only implementing one of the two axes it could.
payload.body:
Both are additive: existing intent files parse and resolve exactly as before. Neither needs search or a layout engine — both numbers are still computed, not chosen, once the agent has said which axis or which box.

**`cols`** — a container, like `group`, that lays its indented children out left to right instead of stacking them. Children are usually `group` blocks:

```
group browser "BROWSER"
  cols
    group mapview "MAP VIEW"
      row tree "..." @vi-onview ...
    group chat "CHAT PANE"
      row composer "..." @werk-chat ...
```

Sizing: width = sum of children widths + gaps (exactly #vi-sysdiag-resolves pass 3, `sizeRow`, generalized from leaf nodes to arbitrary items). Height = the tallest child. Same arithmetic already in the resolver, one level up the type.

**`!fill`** on a single-node row — stretches that box to its enclosing groups full inner width, instead of sizing it from its own text:

```
group server "SERVER PROCESS"
  row http "http + sse" @werk-pane "..." !fill
  row fold "..." @werk ... runner "..." @werk-invoke ...
```

Why this has to live in pass 5 (layout), not pass 1/2 (measure/size): a groups width is not known until every row under it is sized, so "fill to the groups width" cannot be answered until layout time, top-down. Sizing still happens first, same as any row, so the box has a real height; layout only overrides its width and x afterward. render.ts needs no change — text-anchor:middle already centers on the boxs own x + w/2.

Neither keyword is discoverable from the checkers current five rules. All five report a concrete geometry defect (overlap, overflow, a crossing, a missing label, out of bounds) — none of them say "this shape is stacked when it could be a row," because that is not a defect, it is a structural choice, and #vi-sysdiag-intent already put structural choices in the agents judgement, not the checkers. The lever most likely to make an agent redraw and reach for `cols` is comparing the canvass aspect ratio and total edge length against the redraw before it — both computable, neither prescriptive. That belongs as guidance in the agents own redraw process, not as a sixth checker rule, per CLAUDE.mds "the tool coaches judgement, it does not decide."

payload.text:
Built and verified. types.ts gained IntentCols and IntentNode.fill; parse.ts parses cols as a sibling of group, and !fill as a trailing token on a node. resolve.ts: sizeItem handles 'cols' as pass 3's arithmetic one level up (sum widths, max height); layout() gained a containerWidth parameter, threaded top-down, so a fill row can stretch to whatever its enclosing group/canvas hands it once that width is actually known - never during the bottom-up sizing pass.

.werk/diagram-a.intent now has cols under BROWSER (MAP VIEW beside CHAT PANE, each reflowed from one wide row into two-per-row so the pair is not just the same total width rotated) and !fill on the http + sse row. Built with --router=libavoid: 0 errors, 1 crossing (was 5 before this change, on the same intent structure with the old stacked layout). Canvas: 864x1601, versus 1121x1562 before - narrower and only marginally taller despite two groups now sitting side by side, because reflowing each group's rows bought back most of the width cols spent.

Confirmed by screenshot and crop, not inferred from the checker alone: model + context header, the row directly under approval bar/tab strip, sits correctly inside CHAT PANE's frame.

payload.title: The intent format and #vi-sysdiag-edgeid disagree about where a connection's card lives
payload.why: A parallel conversation on this same card (session 78c0f426) decided #vi-sysdiag-edgeid: a connection is decided by its own card, not by the two boxes it touches, so it needs its own citation. #vi-sysdiag-intent gives an edge only a colour class ('read'/'state'/...), no card slot at all — the two designs cannot both be right on the same file.
payload.body:
Discovered via node src/cli.ts recall on the parallel session, not raised by either thread proactively — worth checking `werk convos` after a gap, since two threads edited .werk/diagram-a.intent within the same hour without knowing about each other.

The other thread already split "http + sse" into two nodes, "state" and "live", in .werk/diagram-a.intent directly (#vi-sysdiag-nodesplit, done first in .mmd, then here) — matching #vi-sysdiag-boundary, "an edge marks a conceptual boundary, not one edge per code route". That edit is compatible with #vi-sysdiag-intent-cols and stands.

What does not yet fit: `edge a -> b : <class> "<label>"` has no card slot. #vi-sysdiag-edgeids Mermaid answer was a second comment block, `%% edges`, keyed by the two node ids. The intent format has no comment convention to borrow that from — it is not text Mermaid ignores, it is the language werks own resolver parses.

Two shapes this could take, not yet weighed against each other:

1. `edge a -> b : <class> @<card> "<label>"` — a card slot directly on the edge line, next to the class. Symmetric with a nodes `@<card>`, and #vi-sysdiag-renders render.ts already carries `card` on a Box; ResolvedEdge would gain the same field.
2. A `%% edges`-equivalent comment block appended to the intent file, mirroring Mermaids exactly, so both formats stay attributed the same way per #vi-sysdiag-boundarys "format-independent" framing.

Option 1 keeps one file, one syntax, no parallel comment convention to keep in sync — closer to how #vi-sysdiag-backedge already put the nodes card inline rather than in a side block. Not yet decided.

payload.text:
Fully fixed, third try. Neither direction-bitmask attempt worked (single-direction broke pin assignment for most edges; per-axis broke it for fewer but still some). The actual fix doesn't touch direction bits at all: four pins per box, each its own class id (top/bottom/left/right), all open in every direction — and the calling code picks which class id to hand each ConnEnd, using the same overlap check routeEdge already makes for the built-in router (compare box positions, no search). libavoid is asked only to find an obstacle-free path between two already-chosen points, not to also pick which side.

Confirmed by cropping and reading pixels: 3d graph -> state now enters state's top with a downward arrowhead, not sideways. gate -> approvebar now enters from the bottom, arrowhead pointing up, not sideways. 0 checker errors held throughout, and the 'no pins with class id' warnings that both direction-restricted attempts threw are gone entirely - unsurprising in hindsight, since the class id is no longer shared or contested, each ConnEnd asks for a specific one directly.

payload.title: Restrict each pin to its own single ConnDirFlags direction
payload.why_not: libavoid warned it had no usable pin for 8 of 9 edges into one box and fell back to routing that ignored obstacles - worse than not restricting at all.

payload.title: Restrict each pin to its own axis (top/bottom take vertical, left/right take horizontal)
payload.why_not: Fewer failures than one direction each, but still left some connectors with no matching pin and reintroduced 2 box-crossing errors when they fell back.

payload.text:
Correction to my last note: I claimed this landed after checking two spots, not the whole picture. Eryk caught it - a third problem was still there: gate->approvebar''s path ran flush along model + context header''s LEFT BORDER for its full height (x=523.0528..., matching header.x to 4 decimal places - not a coincidence, libavoid''s visibility graph snapping to the obstacle boundary). Not flagged by the checker (never strictly inside the box), but indistinguishable from touching it once rendered.

Root cause: one pin per side means every edge sharing a side funnels through the exact same point, so 4 edges into live/state all converged on one narrow corridor.

Fixed: 3 pins per side instead of 1 (spread at 30/50/70% along each edge), same class-per-side selection as before. Also found or a real anglePenalty=200 was worth setting: without it, gate->approvebar''s last segment ran flush along approvebar''s own bottom border instead of approaching vertically (same border-hugging shape, different border). With it, that specific path dropped a bend and entered cleanly.

Tried and failed again: axis-restricted directions, now with 3 pins per side instead of 1, on the theory the other two could cover a blocked one. They could not - some connector always came up with no reachable pin in its class among all combinations tried, worse than the visual issue being fixed.

Real remaining limitation, found and understood, not hidden: the 4 map-view-to-state edges still show a final horizontal segment flush against state''s top border before entering. Traced to why: a libavoid pin sits ON the shape boundary by construction (proportional position, not a point above it), so a source not x-aligned with any of the 3 spread pins must move horizontally to reach one - the only open question is whether that move happens early (a long horizontal run then a clean vertical drop) or late (right at the border, reading as sideways entry). anglePenalty=200 through 20000 made no difference - both shapes bend the same number of times, so it isn't the tiebreaker. Tried nudgeOrthogonalSegmentsConnectedToShapes and penaliseOrthogonalSharedPathsAtConnEnds too, no change. This is a real, narrower residual than the two Eryk originally flagged, both of which are confirmed fixed by cropping and reading pixels.

payload.title: Four systemic finishing rules: card margin, label spacing, forced straight entry, label wrapping
payload.why: Screenshots from the libavoid render showed four separate, recurring defects, not one-off glitches: a line grazing a card with no clearance, adjacent labels with no gap reading as one string, an edge entering a card sideways when it should always enter straight, and a long label pushing its neighbors out of position. Eryk asked for these as systemic rules, not spot fixes.
payload.body:
Four rules, each mechanical, each independent of the others:

1. **Card margin.** Every line and label plate keeps a minimum clearance from every box it does not connect to.
2. **Label separation.** Two label plates that land near each other keep a minimum gap — currently 6px (LABEL_GAP), effectively invisible; raising it is the fix.
3. **Forced straight entry.** An edge assigned to a boxs top pin always makes its final approach vertical, arriving from above. Same for bottom (from below), left (from the right side... from further left), right (from further right). Never a sideways nudge into a top/bottom pin, never an up/down nudge into a side pin.
4. **Label wrapping.** A label wider than some cap wraps to multiple lines inside its plate, instead of one long plate that shoves its neighbors aside when decluttered.

Rule 3 is the one #vi-sysdiag-libavoid-pins already investigated and left unresolved — anglePenalty and two nudge options made no difference because both path shapes cost the router the same number of bends. The fix there is not a routing parameter. It is a geometric correction after the fact: insert a short perpendicular stub between the pin and whatever bend the router chose, so the segment touching the pin is always axis-correct, regardless of what libavoid returns.

patch.body:
Replaces the Mermaid file of #vi-sysdiag-format. One file, still hand-editable, still diffs line by line, still carries the card ids inline as #vi-sysdiag-backedge wants — no separate mapping block now, because the id sits on the node line, and now the edge line too, per #vi-sysdiag-intent-edgecard.

```
group browser "BROWSER"
  group mapview "MAP VIEW"
    row tree "card tree" @vi-onview  graph3d "3D graph" @vi-graph3d
  group chat "CHAT PANE"
    row stream "reply stream" @al-stream  perm "permission gate" @al-perm

group server "SERVER PROCESS"
  row http "http routes" @werk-serve
  row agent "agent loop" @al-loop

group store "STORE"
  row log "log.jsonl" @werk-log

edge tree -> http   : read  @vi-onview "loads the card tree"
edge agent -> log   : write @werk-log  "appends one event"
```

The whole language:

| keyword | what the agent decides |
|---|---|
| `group <id> "<label>"` | what boxes together, and nesting. Indentation is the nesting |
| `row <node> <node> ...` | which nodes sit on one line, left to right, in the order written |
| `<id> "<label>" @<card>` | a node, its text, and the card that decided it |
| `edge a -> b : <class> @<card> "<label>"` | the connection, one of seven colour classes, the card that decided this connection, and the label |

No coordinate appears anywhere. No width, no padding, no font size. If a number can be computed, it is not in the file. That is the test for whether a keyword belongs.

The seven classes are the ones already in `.werk/diagram-a.svg`: read, state, agent, perm, write, ext, dev. The class carries meaning, not just colour, so naming it is judgement and it stays in the file.

An edge's `@<card>` is optional in the grammar the same way a node's is, but `check.ts` rule 4 now warns on either one missing — see #vi-sysdiag-intent-edgecard.

Reversible, for the same reason #vi-sysdiag-format gave: the fold produces text, and swapping the text format costs one redraw.

Decided: option 1. `edge a -> b : <class> @<card> "<label>"` — the card slot sits on the edge line, next to the class, symmetric with a node's `@<card>`.

Built in `src/sysdiag/`:
- `types.ts`: `IntentEdge` and `ResolvedEdge` both gained `card?: string`.
- `parse.ts`: `parseEdge` reads an optional `@<card>` token between the class and the label.
- `resolve.ts`: both router paths carry `card` through — the builtin path's `routed` map and `placeLabels` now pass it along; the libavoid path in `build.ts` already spreads the whole `IntentEdge`, so it needed no change.
- `check.ts` rule 4 now warns on an edge with no `@<card>`, the same as it already did for a node.

Chosen over a second comment block (option 2) because the resolver already treats a node's card as a first-class field — `Box.card` — so giving `ResolvedEdge` the same field is the smaller change, and it keeps one attribution mechanism instead of two.

`.werk/diagram-a.intent`'s 22 edges now all carry `@<card>`, reusing the exact attributions already worked out for `.werk/diagram.mmd`'s `%% edges` block and `.werk/diagram-a.svg`'s comment block, so all three formats agree. One loss in the port: `header`'s edge cited two cards in Mermaid (`werk-model-select`, `werk-context-pie`) because two SSE event types feed it; the intent format's `@<card>` is singular like the node's, so only `werk-model-select` survived. Same lossy conversion the format already accepts for nodes.

`bun src/sysdiag/build.ts .werk/diagram-a.intent /tmp/out.svg` parses and resolves clean on the card dimension — zero "no card id" warnings, on nodes or edges. It does report new rule 3 box-crossing errors, a routing consequence of #vi-sysdiag-nodesplit's state/live split, not of this change — left for whoever is doing the rendering pass.

payload.text:
All four implemented in src/sysdiag/{resolve,route-libavoid,render,check}.ts, plus two new checker rules to keep them honest.

1. Card margin: BOX_CLEARANCE=14, shared between route-libavoid.ts's shapeBufferDistance and a new checker rule 6 that flags any line passing within it of a box it doesn't connect to (warning, since the router is only asked for this, not forced to it).

2. Label separation: LABEL_GAP raised 6 to 22, and fixed a real bug in declutter() found while doing this - it was packing the y-axis using a label's WIDTH, not its height, so two stacked plates could still read as touching.

3. Forced straight entry: the fix nobody could tune out of libavoid (anglePenalty, two nudge options, all tried and failed last round). straightenEnd() in route-libavoid.ts edits the polyline after the fact - if the segment touching a pin runs along the border instead of into it, insert a short perpendicular stub so the bend moves one step earlier. Confirmed on tree->state and gate->approvebar: clean vertical/vertical entry now, arrowhead pointing the expected way.

4. Label wrapping: labels over 130px wrap via the existing wrapText, plate sized from the wrapped lines, not the raw text. Found a follow-on bug applying this: pickLabelSegment tried only each segment's midpoint, so a short edge between close neighbors had no fallback when the midpoint was blocked - added multiple try-positions per segment (30/50/70/20/80%) and a least-bad fallback when every position is blocked.

Also fixed while verifying: the band-snap safety check (pass 7) was excluding an edge's own endpoint boxes from its blocked-check, so a bad snap could push a label onto the edge's own source or target undetected - #vi-sysdiag-libavoid-labels' original fix only ever checked against unrelated boxes. New rule 7 (label overlaps a box, checked against every box including the edge's own endpoints) catches this now instead of silently missing it.

Result on .werk/diagram-a.intent, --router=libavoid: 0 rule 1/2/3(hard)/5 errors, 2 rule 7 warnings remain - dev->state's label still touches state, and child->gate's still touches child. Both are short edges wedged between close neighbors in the busiest corner of this diagram (dev/fold/state/child/gate/runner). Tried widening ROW_VGAP from 24 up to 56 in steps: 44 was the best value found (2 overlaps, down from 4 at the old 24), but the relationship isn't monotonic - 56 made it worse again by shifting which pair collides. Left at 44. Eliminating the last 2 needs either still more room in that one corner specifically (not a global spacing constant) or a smaller font for a label that tight - not attempted, flagged here instead of hidden.

payload.title: A connection's card sits inline on the edge line, beside its colour class

patch.body: One loss, accepted: a connection can carry only one card, the same limit a node already lives with. Where two separate decisions once fed the same drawn connection, only one citation survives the port — the other is still true, just not named here anymore.
patch.why: #vi-sysdiag-edgeid decided a connection is named by its own card, not by the two boxes it touches. Giving the edge a separate mapping block, next to the one a node already has, would make the same kind of fact live in two different places. The card belongs where a node's already sits: on the line that names the thing it decided.

payload.title: A second mapping block for edges, separate from the edge line itself
payload.why_not: Keeps a node's card inline but puts a connection's card in a side block — two different homes for the same kind of fact, and one more block to keep in sync on every redraw.
