payload.title: A sampler subagent decides, runs, and reports forks
payload.why: Sampling only happens if something triggers it. Put the when-to-sample call in a subagent the main agent spawns before it asks a question.
payload.body:
Three parts. The judgement lives in the subagent, not in the main prompt.

1. **`.claude/agents/sampler.md`** — prompt text only, per AGENTS.md rule 1. It gets the card id and the brief the main agent is about to build from. It applies #al-sample-when's two tests and may answer `NO SAMPLE — <reason>`. That answer is the common case, not a failure. If both tests pass, it picks the substrate rung (plan, output, screenshot), picks the isolation tier per #al-sample-build-isolation, runs the fan-out, and returns the forks. Same split as `sysdiag-scout`: it reads and reports. It never writes a card.

2. **`node src/cli.ts sample`** — the logic, in the program. `src/sample.ts` already has `sample()` and `findForks()` at the plan rung, but no CLI entry, so nothing can call it. Verb:

   `node src/cli.ts sample --brief-file <path> [--n 3] [--tier plan|output|worktree] [--timeout 300]`

   It prints forks and rejected forks as JSON. Tier `plan` is what exists today. Tier `output` adds a private scratch directory per sample and a build command pointed at it. Tier `worktree` adds #al-ephem's worktree and a `.patch` per sample. Build `plan` and `output` first. Build `worktree` when a source-mutating fork actually appears.

3. **The trigger, in `SYSTEM` (src/agent.ts:147).** One paragraph: before you ask Eryk to choose between readings of a requirement, spawn `sampler` first. The trigger is the question, not the topic. #al-two already says never show one option, so the moment options are needed is the moment to test whether the machine can find them. A `NO SAMPLE` answer returns the main agent to writing the options itself.

**Who writes the cards: the main agent.** The subagent has no conversation context, and option cards need it — #al-two wants diverse options and a short rationale, and "I do not care" is offered live, never written as a node.

**Budget stays in the CLI, not the prompt.** N=3 and the wall-clock cap are enforced by code; a prompt cannot enforce a cap. One fan-out per turn. A second one needs Eryk to say so.

Open: one agent, or the scout/runner split `sysdiag` uses. One agent is fewer moving parts, and the judge needs the brief in context anyway. The split only pays if the judge call must stay cheap.

payload.title: How an out-of-scope area is recorded
payload.why: why_not already works on any kind. The missing half is how the card leaves the open count without pretending it was built. Five shapes, two of them need no new schema.
payload.body:
`why_not` is not the question — it already exists on any `Node` (`src/types.ts:58`), `add` and `edit` take it for any kind (`src/cli.ts:223`, `:354`), and the web renders it as *Not chosen: …* (`web/app.js:313`). The question is what carries the card out of the open count. Five shapes:

### 1. A fourth `Status`

`'decided' | 'open' | 'proto' | 'out-of-scope'`. Explicit and self-documenting. Cost: every switch on status moves — the tile colour (`web/app.js:1579`), the rollup (`src/fold.ts:317`), the `decided` contract check (`src/cli.ts:257`), #rollup, #drained. The widest change of the five.

### 2. `decided` + `why_not`

A negative decision is still a decision: *"we are not doing this, because …"*. Zero schema change. It passes the contract check honestly — an out-of-scope ruling has a `who`, a basis, and usually a weighed option. Cost: `decided` stops meaning "we will do this", and #drained reads a ruled-out subtree as green. That may be correct — it *is* settled — but it is a change to what the colour means.

### 3. `open` + `why_not`

The status quo with a note. It still inflates `open` forever and still blocks `settled` and `drained`. It records the reason and fixes nothing.

### 4. A reopen reason

`werk reopen <id> --reason rejected` already exists (`ReopenReason`, `src/types.ts:12`), and today it does nothing distinct: `deriveStaleness` maps everything except `postponed` to `stale` (`src/fold.ts:240`). Out of scope could become a third mark beside `stale` and `paused`, reusing the whole `flagWhy` trace and the closure walk — see #vi-prop-bornstale. Cost: `reopen` presumes the card was decided. An area ruled out before anyone decided it cannot be reopened.

### 5. An `option` node on the subtree root

An out-of-scope area is an alternative that was weighed and not taken — which is exactly `--kind option --why_not` plus `alternative_to`. **The rollup counts only `kind === 'card'`** (`src/fold.ts:317`, `:336`), so an option is already invisible to `open`, `proto`, and `drained`. Zero schema change, zero new status, and it reuses the shape werk already trusts for recorded contrast. Cost: an option's title reads as a *choice*, not an *area*, and it cannot hold `refines` children — so it fits a leaf, not a ruled-out branch.

### Not a candidate

An `excludes` **edge** from the effort to the card. Scope is relational, so this would be right if werk had per-effort maps. It does not — see #pr-wf-dest. One scope, so one property.

---

**Read:** 2 and 5 are the two that cost nothing. 5 if the ruled-out thing is a leaf, 2 if it has substance and children. 3 is the status quo. 1 and 4 both buy a new concept, and 4 only works for something already decided.

patch.body:
`why_not` is not the question — it already exists on any `Node` (`src/types.ts:58`), `add` and `edit` take it for any kind (`src/cli.ts:223`, `:354`), and the web renders it as *Not chosen: …* (`web/app.js:313`). The question is what carries the card out of the open count. Five shapes:

### 1. A fourth `Status`

`'decided' | 'open' | 'proto' | 'out-of-scope'`. Explicit and self-documenting. Cost: every switch on status moves — the tile colour (`web/app.js:1579`), the rollup (`src/fold.ts:317`), the `decided` contract check (`src/cli.ts:257`), #rollup, #drained. The widest change of the five.

### 2. `decided` + `why_not`

A negative decision is still a decision: *"we are not doing this, because …"*. Zero schema change. It passes the contract check honestly — an out-of-scope ruling has a `who`, a basis, and usually a weighed option. Cost: `decided` stops meaning "we will do this", and #drained reads a ruled-out subtree as green. That may be correct — it *is* settled — but it changes what the colour means.

### 3. `open` + `why_not`

The status quo with a note. It still inflates `open` forever and still blocks `settled` and `drained`. It records the reason and fixes nothing.

### 4. A reopen reason

`werk reopen <id> --reason rejected` already exists (`ReopenReason`, `src/types.ts:12`), and today it does nothing distinct: `deriveStaleness` maps everything except `postponed` to `stale` (`src/fold.ts:240`). Out of scope could become a third mark beside `stale` and `paused`, reusing the `flagWhy` trace and the closure walk — see #vi-prop-bornstale. Cost: `reopen` presumes the card was decided. An area ruled out before anyone decided it cannot be reopened.

### 5. An `option` node on the subtree root

An out-of-scope area is an alternative weighed and not taken — exactly `--kind option --why_not` plus `alternative_to`. The rollup counts only `kind === 'card'` (`src/fold.ts:317`, `:336`), so an option is already invisible to `open`, `proto`, and `drained`. Zero schema change, zero new status, and it reuses the shape werk already trusts for recorded contrast.

### Not a candidate

An `excludes` **edge** from the effort to the card. Scope is relational, so this would be right if werk had per-effort maps. It does not — see #pr-wf-dest. One scope, so one property.

---

## The test: does the ruled-out thing have cards under it?

`deriveRollup` walks `refines` children **regardless of kind** and counts only the cards it passes (`src/fold.ts:336`, `:356`). So an `option` node hides **itself**, not its subtree. That decides which shape fits.

### Nothing under it → shape 5

*Two people edit the map at once.* Never discussed, no card, nothing depends on it, and it is plainly not this effort. Shape 3 would inflate `open` forever. Shape 2 would overstate it — nobody decided anything, there is no basis to record and no contract to satisfy. Shape 5 fits exactly:

```bash
werk add visual:oos0 --kind option --title "Two people edit the map at once" \
  --why_not "Single-author tool. Concurrency is a product problem, not a judgement problem."
werk link visual:oos0 visual --type alternative_to
```

It reads as *Not chosen* on #visual's tile and touches no count.

### Cards under it → shape 2

Suppose #tracker goes out of scope — werk publishes nowhere and `log.jsonl` is the only home. #tracker is not *wrong*; it was decided, and nine decided cards sit under it. Shape 5 cannot hold them: turn #tracker into an option and its nine children still count toward #root's rollup, because the walk does not stop at a non-card. So #tracker stays a `card`, becomes `decided` with `--why_not`, and the nine children stay as the record of how the area was explored. #drained then reads the subtree green — honest, because nothing is left to decide there.

**Rule:** a ruled-out leaf is an `option`. A ruled-out branch is a `decided` card with `why_not`.
patch.why: why_not already works on any kind. The missing half is how the card leaves the open count. Five shapes. The test is whether the ruled-out thing has cards under it: an option node hides itself, not its subtree.

ops.old: Open: one agent, or the scout/runner split `sysdiag` uses. One agent is fewer moving parts, and the judge needs the brief in context anyway. The split only pays if the judge call must stay cheap.
ops.new: Decided: one agent judges and runs the sample fan-out. A second agent, #al-sample-proto-agent, takes its forks up to the next rung. The split is by substrate rung, not by judge-against-run — #al-sample-when's ladder already draws that line, and the plan rung must finish before anything is worth building.

payload.title: A second agent takes each fork up to the built rung
payload.why: The plan rung names the fork. Some forks only become real as a screenshot. One artifact per option, built in parallel.
payload.body:
The second agent in the chain. #al-sample-agent finds the forks at the plan rung. This one asks, per fork, whether prose already settles it — and if not, builds the artifact that makes it visible.

**The unit is an option, not a sample.** N samples cluster into two or three choices per fork. Building one artifact per sample builds duplicates of the same choice. #al-two and #al-ephem both want one artifact per option: a screenshot and a `.patch`, attached as evidence to the option card.

**It may answer `NO BUILD`.** The plan rung often settles the fork on its own. #al-sample-when's first test applies again, one rung up: if two sentences of prose make the choice clear, a running artifact shows nothing new.

**Parallelism lives in code, not in nested subagents.** The agent picks the tier per option per #al-sample-build-isolation, then calls one CLI verb that fans out:

`node src/cli.ts prototype --fork <file> [--tier output|worktree] [--timeout 600]`

Each option gets a private scratch output directory, or a worktree when the option mutates tracked files. The verb returns a screenshot path and a `.patch` per option. Rejected: al-sample-proto-agent:opt0.

The main agent still writes the option cards and attaches the evidence. This agent reads and builds. It never writes a card.

payload.title: The agent spawns one subagent per option to build in parallel
payload.why_not: A Claude Code subagent cannot reliably spawn subagents of its own, so the fan-out would have to climb back to the main agent and fill its context with build noise. Parallel process control is logic, and AGENTS.md rule 1 puts logic in the program.

payload.title: A ruled-out leaf is an option. A ruled-out branch is a decided card with why_not
A fourth Status, 'out-of-scope'
payload.why_not: The widest change of the five, for no information that why_not does not already carry. Every switch on status moves: the tile colour (web/app.js:1579), the rollup (src/fold.ts:317), the decided contract check (src/cli.ts:257), #rollup and #drained. Shapes 2 and 5 cover both real cases with no schema change.

payload.title: Keep the card open, with why_not as a note
payload.why_not: The status quo with a note. It records the reason and fixes nothing: the card still inflates open forever, and it still blocks settled and drained on #drained.

payload.title: A third mark from reopen --reason rejected, beside stale and paused
payload.why_not: reopen presumes the card was decided, so it cannot rule out an area nobody has decided — which is exactly the leaf case. It would also add a third mark for a state that is not a correction: stale and paused both mean 'this may be wrong now', and out of scope means 'this is not ours'.

payload.title: A decided card with why_not needs its own mark
payload.why: Shape 2 makes decided mean two things. Today a ruled-out branch is pixel-identical to a built one: cardHTML renders why ?? finding and never why_not, and classOf switches on status alone.
payload.body:
See #pr-wf-scope for the rule. This card is only about how the ruled-out case reads.

## What it looks like today

| place | code | behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| tile | `cardHTML`, `web/app.js:138` | shows `n.why ?? n.finding`. `why_not` is never rendered. |
| tile class | `classOf`, `web/app.js:111` | `status` plus `is-stale`/`is-paused`. No hook for `why_not`. |
| detail | `web/app.js:313` | prints **Not chosen: …** — option language. Wrong for a branch ruled out of scope: nothing lost a contest. |
| 3D | `baseNodeColor3D`, `web/app.js:1577` | switches on `status` alone. |
| rollup | `deriveRollup`, `src/fold.ts:345` | counts it as `decided`, and as `yours`. |

So a ruled-out #tracker would read as nine decided cards of finished work.

## Proposal, to see before deciding

Follow the precedent already argued for `paused` (`web/app.js:1570`): a mark **on top of** the status colour, never a replacement, so `decided` is not lost. Concretely:

1. `classOf` adds `is-out-of-scope` when `kind === 'card' && why_not`.
2. The tile renders `why_not` in place of `why`, prefixed **Out of scope**, and gets the overlay.
3. The detail panel says **Out of scope:** for a `card` and keeps **Not chosen:** for an `option`. One string, split by kind.
4. 3D: overlay, same as the paused hatch.
5. Open: does the rollup keep counting it as `decided`? #pr-wf-scope argued green is honest — nothing is left to decide. If the tile carries the mark, the count can stay as it is.

Build 1–4 and look at it. The overlay is not decidable by talking.

payload.title: Paused is about the clock. Out of scope is about the boundary
payload.why: Both leave a card that nobody is working on. Paused says the decision still holds and work comes later. Out of scope says there is no work waiting.
payload.body:
They read alike on the map and come from opposite places. Five differences, all checkable in the code.

| | paused | out of scope |
|---|---|---|
| **truth** | the card still holds. Only execution is deferred | the card is not a pending decision at all |
| **origin** | derived, never authored — `deriveStaleness` computes it from a `reopen --reason postponed` on some origin (`src/fold.ts:239-241`) | authored on the node itself, as `why_not` |
| **graph** | travels the reverse `depends_on` closure: cards that **need** the paused one | covers the `refines` subtree: cards that **sit under** the ruled-out one |
| **return** | expected. `rederive` clears it, and the origin's reopen will be resolved | only if the scope is redrawn, and then as fresh work, not a resumption |
| **count** | keeps its status and is counted in `open`/`proto`/`decided` **and** `paused` (`src/fold.ts:340-354`), so status is never lost | a leaf leaves the counts as an `option`; a branch stays `decided` — see #pr-wf-scope |

## The test

**Is there work waiting behind it?** Paused: yes, later. Out of scope: no, ever.

#pr-logic is the paused example and it is exactly right — "logic in a program, Markdown holds prompts" is still the answer. Only the engine build is deferred, and the mark reached four hops down to #vi-oos-render. If #pr-logic were *out of scope*, the claim itself would leave the map, and the whole `pr-*` subtree with it.

## Why neither one is a status

A werk status describes the **decision**, not the build. #tracker is `decided` with nine decided cards under it, and nothing is published yet — that is not a contradiction, and it is not paused either, because no reopen fired. This is the same reason `paused` had to be a derived mark drawn on top of the status colour instead of replacing it (`web/app.js:1570`), and the reason #pr-wf-scope did not take a fourth `Status`.

payload.why: Eryk collapsed the concept: postponed = paused = out of scope, all mean 'we do not build it now'. So out of scope needs no new mechanism, and why_not on a card has no remaining use case. The leaf/branch rule is moot.

payload.title: A ruled-out leaf is an option node. A ruled-out branch is a decided card with why_not
payload.why_not: Built on the premise that out of scope is a third state, distinct from postponed. It is not — both mean 'we do not build it now'. The rule also needed why_not on a card, which has no remaining use case, and it split one idea across two shapes by subtree size.

payload.title: Out of scope is postponed. There is no third state

patch.body:
**Never say never.** Wayfinder's Out of scope reads as permanent, and it is not: after a few iterations the plan changes. So it maps to *we do not build it now*, which werk already has.

## The mechanism, unchanged

```bash
werk reopen <id> --reason postponed --why "..."
```

`deriveStaleness` fans `postponed` out along the reverse `depends_on` closure as `paused`, not `stale` (`src/fold.ts:239-241`). That closure is the point: if X is not being built, nothing that needs X can be built either. #pr-logic is the live case — the mark reaches four hops down.

## The never-case already has two shapes

1. `werk reopen <id> --reason rejected` — the content is wrong, so the mark is red.
2. Decide the opposite on the card, and keep the original as an `option` with `--why_not` linked `alternative_to`. The normal recorded-contrast shape.

Nothing is missing, so nothing is built. See #pr-wf-paused for the one distinction that stays real: postponed versus rejected.

## Why the open count is not a problem after all

A postponed card keeps its status and still counts in `open`, so a subtree holding one never reads `drained`. That is correct — it *does* have something left to decide, later. And the reader can already see it: `deriveRollup` tracks `openPaused`, `protoPaused` and `decidedPaused` separately (`src/fold.ts:341-347`) and the bar draws the postponed portion inside each status band (`web/app.js:60-62`).

This was the hole that made a fourth `Status` look necessary. It was already filled.

## What is left

One rename, for one word per meaning — see #pr-wf-naming. The reason is `postponed` and the derived mark is `paused`: two words for the same state.
patch.why: Wayfinder's Out of scope means 'we do not build it now', not 'never'. Plans change after a few iterations. That is what reopen --reason postponed already does, and its dependency closure is the reason it works.

payload.title: Rename the derived mark from paused to postponed
payload.why: The reopen reason is postponed and the mark it produces is paused. Two words for one state, and the map shows the word that was never typed.
payload.body:
`ReopenReason` is `'postponed' | 'invalidated' | 'rejected'` (`src/types.ts:12`). The mark it fans out is called `paused` everywhere else. You type `--reason postponed` and the map answers `PAUSED`.

One word per meaning. Rename the mark.

## Scope

| file | occurrences of `paused` |
|---|---|
| `src/fold.ts` | 26 — the `paused` set, `deriveStaleness`'s return, the `Rollup` counters |
| `web/app.js` | 36 — `G.paused`, `classOf`'s `is-paused`, `.ring.paused`, the hover titles |
| `src/cli.ts` | 14 — the `reopen` output and the `show` trace |
| `src/types.ts` | 11 — `Rollup.paused`, `openPaused`, `protoPaused`, `decidedPaused` |
| `web/style.css` | 9 |

Mechanical. No behaviour changes. `stale` keeps its name: `invalidated` and `rejected` both produce it, so no single reason word fits it, and `stale` is the honest description of the state rather than the act.

## The one argument for keeping two words

It was deliberate, not drift — see the comment at `src/fold.ts:217`. *Postponed* names the **act**, and only the origin was postponed. *Paused* names the **state** of a dependent four hops away that nobody touched. After the rename, #vi-oos-render will read "postponed", which is not something anyone did to it.

Accepted anyway: the trace already says where the mark came from and how far away it is — #vi-prop-bornstale built exactly that. The word does not have to carry it.

payload.title: Keep paused for the mark and postponed for the reason
payload.why_not: The distinction is real — postponed is the act, paused is the state of a dependent nobody touched — but it costs a second word for one idea, and the flagWhy trace from #vi-prop-bornstale already names the origin and the hop count. The word does not have to carry that.

payload.title: Paused is about the clock; out of scope is about the boundary
payload.why_not: Assumed out of scope is a separate state from postponed. #pr-wf-scope collapsed them: both mean 'we do not build it now'. The surviving distinction is postponed against rejected.

payload.title: Postponed means not now. Rejected means wrong

patch.body:
The distinction that survives #pr-wf-scope. Out of scope is not a third state — but *not now* and *wrong* are two, and `reopen` already separates them.

| | `--reason postponed` | `--reason rejected` / `invalidated` |
|---|---|---|
| the content | still true | now wrong |
| the mark it fans out | `paused` — calm, keeps the status colour | `stale` — red |
| where it goes | the reverse `depends_on` closure, both cases (`src/fold.ts:239-241`) | same closure |
| a conflict | if two reopens disagree on one dependent, **stale wins** — a real invalidation is never allowed to look calm (`src/fold.ts:219`) | |
| return | expected. `rederive` clears it when work resumes | only by deciding the opposite, which is a new decision |

## The test

**Would you build it unchanged if you had the time?** Postponed: yes. Rejected: no, it would come back different.

#pr-logic is the postponed case and it is exactly right — "logic in a program, Markdown holds prompts" is still the answer. Only the engine build is deferred, and the mark reached four hops down to #vi-oos-render.

## Neither one is a status

A werk status describes the **decision**, not the build. #tracker is `decided` with nine decided cards under it and nothing published yet. That is not a contradiction, and it is not postponed either, because no reopen fired. Same reason the mark is drawn on top of the status colour instead of replacing it (`web/app.js:1570`), and the reason #pr-wf-scope refused a fourth `Status`.
patch.why: Both reopen reasons leave a card nobody is working on. Postponed keeps the content true and fans out a calm mark. Rejected says the content is wrong and fans out the red one.

payload.why: Premise gone. #pr-wf-scope removed why_not from cards, so there is no decided-card-with-why_not to render. A postponed card already reads distinctly: the hatch on the status band from openPaused/protoPaused/decidedPaused (web/app.js:60-62) and the ring on the rollup line. The only fix left is the word, in #pr-wf-naming.

patch.body:
## What the destination actually is

A real named goal, written as one or two lines on the map body. Its *type* is constrained: "the spec, decision, or change this effort is finding its way to." So usually the planning artifact — "a spec for a tool doing X, ready to hand off" — not "the tool doing X". Not always: the skill allows "a change made in place like a data-structure migration", and an effort can carry execution into the map through its Notes.

But naming the goal is not what the destination is *for*. It does two jobs:

1. **A stopping rule.** The map is done when nothing is left to decide. Then the map closes and is thrown away.
2. **A scope boundary.** "Fog only ever gathers toward the destination." Out of scope exists only because a finish line exists.

## Why #root cannot do that job

#root is a thesis. Every card refines it, and it is never reached — you cannot be finished with "we build and fix software with agents in one repeating pipeline." A wayfinder map is an **effort**: disposable, with a finish line. werk's tree is a permanent belief structure. They are different objects that both sit at the top.

So *destination as named goal* is redundant here. #root already does it.

## The plan/build split does not transfer

werk plans by prototyping and then builds, in loops. Wayfinder's split is real for wayfinder because it is a one-shot planning campaign that ends in a handoff. werk has no handoff. So the finish line, if werk gets one, is **per subtree or per loop**, not per map.

## Job 2 is closed

Out of scope needed nothing new: it is `reopen --reason postponed` — see #pr-wf-scope. One rename is left, in #pr-wf-naming.

## Job 1 is what is left

**A finish line per subtree.** #drained is the closest: settled, and unchallenged is zero. It counts; it does not judge. Nothing on the map says "#align is finished when we can sample ambiguity on a real brief." Open: is that a field on the subtree root, or is it what `why` should already be doing?
patch.why: Wayfinder's Destination is a named goal whose job is a stopping rule. #root is a thesis that is never reached. Out of scope turned out to need nothing — see #pr-wf-scope. The finish line is what is left.

patch.body:
**Rejected 2026-09-19.** #pr-wf-scope removed the premise: no card carries `why_not`, so there is no decided-card-with-why_not to mark. The need behind this card — seeing that something is not being built — is already met in five places: `.card.is-paused` (`web/style.css:544`), `.hero.is-paused` (`:505`), the `bar-paused` hatch inside the status band (`:551`), `.ring.paused` on the rollup line (`:370`), and `.tag.paused` / `.depwhy.paused` (`:526`, `:573`). Only the word is wrong — see #pr-wf-naming.

Kept below as the record of what was surveyed.

---

See #pr-wf-scope for the rule. This card is only about how the ruled-out case reads.

## What it looks like today

payload.title: How a subtree says when it is finished
payload.why: drained measures the map, not the world: settled plus unchallenged zero. Nothing says 'align is finished when we can sample ambiguity on a real brief'. Four shapes, three of them free.
payload.body:
#drained is the closest thing today: settled (`r.open + r.proto === 0`) and `r.unchallenged === 0`. Both are **counts over the graph**. Neither can carry an authored, falsifiable condition about the world.

Worth saying first: `why` does not already do this. #align's why is *"the research says options beat descriptions"* — a justification for existing, not a condition for stopping.

### 1. Nothing. `drained` is the finish line

werk loops. Step 6 reopens step 1, so a subtree is never *finished*, only quiet for now. A finish line per subtree may be the same category error as a destination on #root, one level down. Free. Cost: the map can say nothing is left *on the map*, never whether it asked enough — which is #drained's own `why`, unanswered.

### 2. A `done_when` field on the card

One authored line beside `why`, on any card. Cheapest authored shape. Cost: nothing computes it, nothing checks it, and it rots silently — the failure mode #pr-now hit when it copied #tk-verbs' count.

### 3. The finish line is a card

A child of the subtree root whose **title is the condition**: *"#align is finished when a real brief runs through the sampler."* It sits `open` until met, then `decided`.

Zero schema change, and it is **blocking for free**: an unmet finish line is an open descendant, so the subtree cannot read as settled. It shows on the tile, it takes a `who`, and it can be reopened when the loop comes round — which is exactly what step 6 does to it.

This is already half-true. `settled` requires `proto === 0`, so any `--who prototype` card is a blocking finish line today: *you are not done while something must be built to find out.*

Open under this shape: does it need its own `kind` so the tile reads *finish line* instead of an ordinary open decision, or is a title convention enough?

### 4. A fifth rollup number

Shape 2 or 3, plus `deriveRollup` computing *finished*. Real cost: `src/fold.ts`, `Rollup` in `src/types.ts`, the bar and the line in `web/app.js`. Buys a colour for something a single open card already expresses under shape 3.

---

**Read: 3.** A finish line is a judgement — *have we met the bar?* — and werk's unit for a judgement is a card. It costs nothing, it blocks by construction, and it survives the loop. 1 is the honest do-nothing and the only one that argues the need away. 2 is invisible to every computation. 4 pays schema for a colour.

patch.body:
#drained is the closest thing today: settled (`r.open + r.proto === 0`) and `r.unchallenged === 0`. Both are **counts over the graph**. Neither can carry an authored, falsifiable condition about the world.

Worth saying first: `why` does not already do this. #align's why is *"the research says options beat descriptions"* — a justification for existing, not a condition for stopping.

Every example below uses the same real subtree and the same bar. **#align** reads *10 cards, 1 open, 1 proto, 8 decided, 3 unchallenged*, and the bar is: *a real brief runs through the sampler, and the forks it reports are ones Eryk agrees are real.*

### 1. Nothing. `drained` is the finish line

You read the rollup line and infer it. Today #align shows `1 open, 1 proto`; the proto is #al-sample, and `--who prototype` already means *build it first*. When those two close, the line reads `10 decided` and the branch is quiet.

Nothing on screen ever said what the bar was. If #al-sample flips to decided because the idea got dropped rather than tested, the branch reads identical.

werk loops — step 6 reopens step 1 — so a subtree is never *finished*, only quiet for now. Free, and the only shape that argues the need away.

### 2. A `done_when` field on the card

```bash
werk edit align --done_when "A real brief runs through the sampler, and the forks it reports are ones you agree are real."
```

One authored line under `why` on the hero. Cheapest authored shape, and the whole of it: #align still reads settled the moment the last card closes, whether or not a brief ever ran. Nothing computes it, nothing checks it, and it rots silently — the failure #pr-now hit when it copied #tk-verbs' count.

### 3. The finish line is a card

```bash
werk add al-finish --parent align --status proto --who prototype \
  --title "A real brief runs through the sampler, and its forks are ones you agree are real" \
  --why "The bar for #align. Until a real requirement produces forks Eryk recognises, the sampling claim is untested."
werk link al-finish al-sample --type depends_on
```

#align now reads `1 open, 2 proto` and **cannot** read settled until someone runs a brief and judges the result. Blocking for free — no new computation, the existing `settled` rule does it.

The `depends_on` matters: if #al-sample is invalidated, the bar goes stale with it. A finish line is not independent of the claim it tests. When step 6 comes round with a worse result, `werk reopen al-finish`.

This is already half-true today. `settled` requires `proto === 0`, so any `--who prototype` card is a blocking finish line: *you are not done while something must be built to find out.* Shape 3 only makes the bar explicit instead of implied.

Open under this shape: does it need its own `kind` so the tile reads *finish line* instead of an ordinary open decision, or is a title convention enough?

### 4. A fifth rollup number

#root's line gains `3 finished, 1 unfinished`, and the bar gains a band. But `deriveRollup` has to know **which** node holds the bar, so it needs shape 2 or 3 underneath it first. It is never standalone — it is a renderer on top of one of the others, paying `src/fold.ts`, `Rollup` in `src/types.ts`, and the bar and line in `web/app.js` for a colour that one open card already expresses.

---

**Read: 3.** A finish line is a judgement — *have we met the bar?* — and werk's unit for a judgement is a card. It costs nothing, it blocks by construction, it carries a `who`, and it survives the loop.

payload.text:
Yes, but that sentence states the trade-off too generously to shape 1. The loop is not the question.

Between two reopenings there is a real difference between 'we stopped because we tested it' and 'we stopped because nobody raised anything'. The loop re-crosses the bar; it does not erase the difference. Today those two read identical.

That is the same move #drained already made, one level down. #drained exists because all-green could not tell 'one decision, unchallenged' from 'many decisions, each contested', and 'unchallenged' was the fix. A finish line is the identical fix against a different blind spot: drained cannot tell 'decided and tested against the world' from 'decided and never tried'.

So shape 1's argument is inconsistent with a ruling already on the map. If 'the loop means nothing is ever finished, do not model it' holds, then 'the loop means any decision may be re-contested, do not count unchallenged' holds too. That was rejected.

The honest cost on the other side, which is what you are really accepting or not:

- unchallenged is computed from the graph — was an option recorded? — so it cannot lie. A finish line is authored prose about the world, so it can rot. Shape 3 blunts this by making it a card with a who: someone has to decide the bar is met.
- A bar nobody ever runs sits open forever and makes the branch permanently unsettled. Shape 1 has no such failure mode.

Elaborating both branches — and it changes my recommendation.

## If you take 3

You commit to writing a bar for every subtree that makes a claim about the world. If only some carry one, 'no bar' is ambiguous: none needed, or nobody wrote one? That is the exact ambiguity unchallenged was invented to kill, reappearing one level up. So shape 3 needs a companion marker like --no-basis: 'this branch needs no bar'. It is free in schema, not free in semantics.

Expect the first version to fire too often. #ro-unchal went from 44 of 49 to a usable count only after it was narrowed to who:you.

One real protection: a bar is a card, so it inherits staleness through depends_on. Rot is visible, unlike a field.
Failure mode: bars nobody runs leave branches permanently unsettled, and settled stops meaning anything.

## If you keep 1, you are not choosing nothing

I under-sold this. The per-card version of 'tested' already exists:

- --kind source --finding plus a supported_by edge records the evidence.
- cardHTML already prints 'N evidence' on the tile (web/app.js:126).
- werk dispute <source> flags every citer for review, one hop (src/fold.ts:371).

So a decided card with zero evidence already reads as untested, per card, today.

What is genuinely missing is only the subtree view: Rollup has no evidence count (src/types.ts:105-116), and supported_by appears in fold.ts once, for deriveNeedsReview. Adding an 'evidenced' number to the rollup is smaller than shape 3 and reuses a mechanism that already carries dispute and review.

## The narrower question

A source is backward-looking: here is evidence for this claim. A bar is forward-looking: here is what we must cross. Only shape 3 gives the second.

Revised read: roll evidence up first. It costs one number, needs no new authoring on any existing card, and answers tested-against-untested for the whole map at once. Add shape 3 later, only where the bar has to be named before the work rather than recognised after it — which is a much smaller set of branches than 'every subtree'.

payload.title: Finished for now = every card decided and every prototype built. The pipeline takes that, minus postponed

patch.body:
No authored bar. Discussing a topic always uncovers more detail, so *when to stop* is arbitrary — writing the stopping point down does not make it less arbitrary, it just fixes one guess in place.

## Two reading rules, no new code

```
finished (for now)   r.open + r.proto === 0
buildable            (r.open - r.openPaused) + (r.proto - r.protoPaused) === 0
```

**Finished** is `settled`, which already exists: every card decided, and `proto === 0` means every prototype has been built and judged. A `--who prototype` card is `proto` until it is built, so "all prototypes built" needs nothing beyond the status it already has.

**Buildable** is the same thing with postponed children excluded. A postponed card is not work remaining — it is work deliberately not being done — so it must not hold the branch back. `deriveRollup` already tracks `openPaused` and `protoPaused` per status (`src/fold.ts:341-344`), so both numbers are there.

Neither needs a field, a card, a `kind`, or a `Rollup` entry. Same shape as #drained: nothing was built for that either — it is two existing numbers read together.

## Finished is weaker than drained, on purpose

| | rule | what it answers |
|---|---|---|
| buildable | settled, ignoring postponed | can the build loop start? |
| finished / settled | `open + proto === 0` | is any work left? |
| drained | settled and `unchallenged === 0` | were the decisions contested? — #drained |

Finished does not require `unchallenged === 0`. It is a work-remaining line, not a quality line. Drained stays the quality line.

## Why no authored bar

Shape 3 — a bar as a card — was the alternative. It would have needed a bar on every subtree making a claim about the world, plus a "needs no bar" marker to keep "no bar" from being ambiguous, plus narrowing after the first version over-fired the way #ro-unchal did at 44 of 49. All of that to fix one arbitrary stopping point in place. See #pr-wf-finish:opt0.
patch.why: An authored finish line is an arbitrary stopping point: discussion always finds more detail. So no bar is written. Finished is read off the rollup, and the build pipeline reads the same thing with postponed children excluded.

payload.title: Write the bar as a card under the subtree root
payload.why_not: An authored finish line fixes one arbitrary guess in place. Discussion always finds more detail, so the bar would be rewritten more often than it is crossed. It also needs a companion 'needs no bar' marker, or 'no bar' cannot be told from 'nobody wrote one'.

payload.title: A done_when field on the card
payload.why_not: Same arbitrary guess as the card version, with none of its protections: no who to decide the bar is met, no staleness through depends_on, and nothing computes it. It rots silently.

payload.title: A fifth Rollup number for finished
payload.why_not: Pays src/fold.ts, Rollup, and both renderers for a value that is two existing numbers read together. Same reason nothing was built for #drained.

payload.title: werk needs neither a destination nor an out-of-scope. Both jobs are already done

patch.body:
Wayfinder's **Destination** is a named goal — "the spec, decision, or change this effort is finding its way to" — but naming the goal is not what it is *for*. It does two jobs:

1. **A stopping rule.** The map is done when nothing is left to decide. Then the map closes and is thrown away.
2. **A scope boundary.** "Fog only ever gathers toward the destination." Out of scope exists only because a finish line exists.

Both are now closed, and neither needed anything built.

## Job 1 — the stopping rule

#root is a thesis, never reached: you cannot be finished with "we build and fix software with agents in one repeating pipeline." A wayfinder map is an **effort** — disposable, with a finish line. werk's tree is a permanent belief structure. Different objects that both sit at the top, so *destination as named goal* is redundant.

And the plan/build split does not transfer: wayfinder is a one-shot planning campaign ending in a handoff, werk plans by prototyping and then builds, in loops. So the stopping rule is per subtree, not per map — and it is a reading rule over the existing rollup, not an authored bar. See #pr-wf-finish.

## Job 2 — the scope boundary

Out of scope is not a third state. It means *we do not build it now*, which is `reopen --reason postponed`, and its `depends_on` closure is the reason it works. See #pr-wf-scope. One rename is left, in #pr-wf-naming.

## What wayfinder keeps that werk does not copy

The disposable map. An effort that closes and is thrown away has a finish line by definition. werk's map outlives every effort, so it trades that clarity for a record that survives the loop.
patch.why: The destination's two jobs are a stopping rule and a scope boundary. #root plus the rollup cover the first, reopen --reason postponed covers the second. Nothing to add.

payload.title: Client framework: React + Vite
payload.why: Eryk decided. Criterion 2 (state-preserving per-component HMR) and criterion 6 (agent proficiency) both point at React, and neither runner-up wins them back.

payload.title: Hydration pattern: islands, not Astro or RSC
payload.why: Eryk decided. The server already holds the fold and renders card HTML directly. React roots mount only where state lives, which buys partial hydration without an MPA model that would fight the chat pane.

payload.title: React Server Components (RSC)
payload.why_not: Answers criteria 3 and 4 natively, but needs Waku, Parcel-RSC, or an equivalent on a custom Bun server — bleeding edge in exactly the layer that must not break. Hand-rolled islands get most of the benefit with none of that risk. Revisit only if the manual-roots approach proves insufficient, and record it as a reopen with a reason.

patch.body:
React + Vite. Vite runs as the CLIENT dev server, in middleware mode, inside werk's own Bun server. It is not the server runtime — that is why this does not contradict #werk-hmr, which rejected **vite-node as the process host** after it crashed werk outright (#werk-hmr:src2). One process: Bun serves the API and the SSE stream and hot-reloads its own modules. Vite transforms and hot-reloads the client.

## Why, against the six criteria

1. **Component architecture** — React. Every candidate satisfied this.
2. **Per-component HMR preserving state** — the discriminator. React Fast Refresh preserves hook state per component. It is the most proven implementation of this requirement. Every rejected option lost or weakened it: Lit has no equivalent (#werk-stack:opt0), Solid remounts (#werk-stack:opt2), svelte-hmr is less reliable for the case that matters (#werk-stack:opt3). werk's chat pane holds a live SSE stream and an in-flight turn. A remount on save is the failure this criterion exists to prevent.
6. **Agent proficiency** — React by a wide margin. Eryk ranked this alongside criterion 2. It is why the Svelte 5 runner-up lost: runes are recent enough that agents still reach for Svelte 4 store idioms.

Criteria 3, 4, and 5 do not discriminate between frameworks — see #werk-stack-hydration and #werk-hmr.

The three rejected options are #werk-stack:opt0, #werk-stack:opt2, #werk-stack:opt3, each with its own why_not.

Islands as a pattern, not a platform: multiple small React roots inside server-rendered HTML. Not Astro, not RSC.

    hydrated            the chat pane, the tab strip (#werk-mc-tabs), the ask bar,
                        the map controls, the 3D graph view
    never hydrated      the card body, rendered Markdown, the evidence and
                        depends-on lists, breadcrumbs, rollup bars

## Why, against the six criteria

3. **Progressive loading** — not solved by the hydration pattern. See #werk-stack-api. The API is card-scoped from day one. React's role is only that Suspense boundaries make a card-at-a-time fetch natural to express.
4. **Partial hydration for static content** — solved by the islands list above. The server already holds the fold, so it server-renders card HTML that never hydrates. This buys criterion 4 without the MPA model that fights the chat pane: werk's chat pane holds a live SSE stream and an in-flight turn that must survive every card navigation.

## Rejected options

**#werk-stack-hydration:opt-rsc — RSC.** It answers criteria 3 and 4 natively, but it needs Waku, Parcel-RSC, or an equivalent on a custom Bun server — bleeding edge in exactly the layer that must not break. Hand-rolled islands get most of the benefit with none of that risk.

**#werk-stack:opt1 — Astro with islands.** Moved here from #werk-stack. Astro is page-oriented: a navigation is a document swap. That is the one thing an MPA model makes hardest for werk's chat pane. Astro island HMR also tends to remount the island, losing criterion 2 exactly where state matters most.

Eryk decided this. A new implementation is built on this stack from scratch — this card is not a migration plan, and nothing here asks anyone to port web/app.js.

Two separate choices, each decided on its own card:

    framework    React + Vite              #werk-stack-framework
    hydration    islands as a pattern      #werk-stack-hydration

Runtime (Bun, bun --hot) was already decided at #werk-hmr. Progressive loading is an API shape decision, not a framework feature — see #werk-stack-api.
